answer: Measured-boot kernel identity stops sybil farms at the inlet. First, an agent boots a signed kernel and records its kernel, initramfs, and enclave hashes in a tamper-proof log. Second, it sends that log plus a fresh nonce to the registry, which checks the hashes against an approved list. Third, peers re-measure the agent every 7 days, and any mismatch revokes its credential within one hour, before it can trade. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real machines at $400 each, $400,000, plus 7,000 days of upkeep. Like a glacier, trust here moves slowly and crushes shortcuts.
